healthcare.summary: Health & medication guide for Poland. Emergency numbers (112/999/997/998), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, travel insurance advice, and vaccination recommendations.
healthcare.costForTourists: Public healthcare is available to EU citizens with an EHIC card. Non-EU tourists will typically use private clinics where a GP visit costs around $30–$60 and specialist consultations $50–$100 — very affordable by Western European standards.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance is recommended for all visitors. EU/EEA citizens should bring their EHIC for public healthcare access; non-EU visitors should ensure private medical coverage as public hospitals may refuse non-emergency treatment without insurance.
healthcare.vaccinationsRecommended: No special vaccinations required. Routine vaccinations should be up to date. Tick-borne encephalitis vaccine is recommended if planning outdoor activities in forested areas, particularly in northeastern Poland.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Private clinics (such as Medicover, Lux Med, and Enel-Med) in major cities offer good to excellent care with English-speaking staff and short wait times. Public hospitals can have long waits but provide competent emergency care.

medications.prescriptionRules: EU prescriptions are accepted. Prescriptions from outside the EU require a Polish doctor to re-issue them. Some medications available by prescription in other countries may be OTC in Poland.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires prescription in Poland. Small personal-use quantities may be brought with proper documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription or doctor consultation. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. EU regulations apply. Carry doctor's letter and original prescription and packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin) and ADHD stimulants
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires documentation and possibly special permission. Contact Polish health authorities if traveling with ADHD medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal for recreational use. Medical cannabis is legal but strictly regulated. CBD products with no THC are legal and widely available.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in Polish or English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. EU citizens should carry EHIC. Non-EU travelers should carry original prescriptions and multilingual medical certificates.
medications.generalAdvice: Poland follows EU regulations on medication imports. Travelers may bring personal supplies of prescription medication with a valid prescription or doctor's letter, ideally in the original packaging. For narcotics and psychotropic medications, carry a Schengen certificate issued by your home country's health authority. Common OTC medications are readily available at pharmacies (apteka), which are widespread in cities and towns.

cultural.tipping: 10% at restaurants is customary. Round up for taxis. Not expected at bars for simple drinks. Say 'reszta dla pana/pani' (keep the change).
cultural.dressCode: Smart casual in cities. Cover shoulders and knees in churches. Poland is quite fashionable — avoid looking too touristy.
cultural.greetings: Handshake with eye contact. Close friends kiss on both cheeks. Use Pan (Mr) / Pani (Mrs) until invited to use first names. Poles value politeness.
taboos: Confusing Poland with Russia or calling it Eastern Europe (it's Central Europe)

cultural.haggling: Not practiced. Prices are fixed at shops, restaurants, and most markets.

soloFemaleSafety.note: Poland is generally safe for solo female travelers, with major cities well-lit and public transport reliable; standard nightlife precautions apply, particularly regarding drink safety in clubs.

lgbtSafety.note: While homosexuality is legal, Poland has seen a rise in anti-LGBT rhetoric, some municipalities declared 'LGBT-free zones' (since largely reversed), and public displays of affection between same-sex couples may attract hostility outside major cities.

safety.naturalDisasters: Poland occasionally experiences flooding, particularly in southern regions along the Vistula and Oder rivers during heavy spring rains. Severe winter storms can disrupt transport, but natural disaster risk is generally low.
safety.pettyCrime: Pickpocketing and bag theft occur in major cities, particularly in Warsaw, Kraków, and on public transport and at train stations. Drink spiking has been reported in nightlife areas.
safety.violentCrime: Violent crime against tourists is uncommon. Occasional incidents of football hooliganism and racially motivated attacks have been reported, particularly against people of color or visibly foreign appearance.
safety.notes: Poland is a safe and popular European destination with a well-developed tourist infrastructure. Scams targeting tourists (overcharging at restaurants and bars, fake taxis) exist but are declining. Emergency services (112) are reliable, and English is widely spoken by younger Poles in cities.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free (Schengen). UK, EU, Australia, Canada, Japan also visa-free.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: May-September (warm, long days). June-August peak season. December for Christmas markets. Avoid November (grey, cold).

healthcare.summary: Health & medication guide for Czech Republic. Emergency numbers (155/158/150/112), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, travel insurance, and vaccination recommendations.
healthcare.costForTourists: EU/EEA citizens with a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) can access public healthcare at reduced cost. Non-EU tourists should expect to pay for treatment, with consultations typically costing €50-100 and hospital stays significantly more.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: EU citizens should carry an EHIC card. Non-EU travelers should have comprehensive travel insurance, as healthcare costs without coverage can be substantial. Most private clinics require payment upfront.
healthcare.vaccinationsRecommended: No special vaccinations are required. Routine vaccinations should be up to date. Tick-borne encephalitis vaccine is recommended if planning outdoor activities in forested areas, especially during spring and summer.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Prague has several excellent hospitals including Motol University Hospital and Na Homolce Hospital, with some English-speaking staff. Outside Prague, hospital quality remains good but English availability decreases significantly.

Be wary of unofficial currency exchange booths offering suspiciously good rates, and always agree on taxi fares in advance or use apps like Bolt or Liftago.

scams.name: Taxi overcharging
scams.description: Unofficial taxis at Bucharest Henri Coanda Airport and train stations use tampered meters or flat-rate scams charging 10-20x the legitimate fare.
scams.avoidance: Use Bolt or Uber app from the airport. Official taxis have yellow background license plates and rates clearly posted. Avoid touts inside the terminal.

scams.name: Pickpocketing on public transport
scams.description: Pickpockets operate on the Bucharest metro, trams, and buses, working in teams to distract victims while stealing wallets and phones.
scams.avoidance: Keep valuables in front pockets or a zipped bag. Be especially alert at crowded metro stations (Piata Victoriei, Piata Unirii) and on the 40 bus from the airport.

scams.name: Friendly locals with free drink scam
scams.description: Tourists are befriended by locals who invite them to a bar, then receive an exorbitant bill for drinks. Leaving without paying may be prevented by intimidation.
scams.avoidance: Choose your own bar rather than following new acquaintances. Check menus and prices before ordering. Research reputable venues in advance.

scams.name: Currency exchange rate scam
scams.description: Unofficial money changers offer excellent exchange rates but use sleight of hand to short-change tourists or add hidden commissions after the deal.
scams.avoidance: Use official exchange offices (casa de schimb) or bank ATMs only. Compare rates online before exchanging. Count all bills carefully before leaving the counter.

scams.name: Stray dog attacks
scams.description: Stray dogs remain a problem in rural areas and some parts of cities. They can be aggressive in packs, particularly around waste areas.
scams.avoidance: Do not approach stray dogs. If confronted, avoid direct eye contact and back away slowly. Carry a walking stick in rural areas.

cultural.tipping: Expected in restaurants: 10-15%. Leave cash on table or hand directly to waiter. Hotel staff: 5-10 RON per service. Taxi drivers: round up. Not obligatory but greatly appreciated.
cultural.dressCode: Casual dress acceptable most places. Smart casual for restaurants. Cover shoulders and knees when visiting Orthodox churches. Remove hats inside churches.
cultural.greetings: Handshakes common for business introductions. Friends and family greet with cheek kisses. 'Bună ziua' (good day) is a polite greeting. Romanians are generally warm and hospitable.

cultural.haggling: Not typical in shops, restaurants, or markets. Fixed prices generally observed. Some negotiation possible in informal markets or for larger purchases.

safety.lgbtSafety: Same-sex relationships are legal but Romania has limited legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals. Public acceptance is lower than Western Europe, especially in rural areas. Bucharest Pride occurs annually but with some opposition.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Generally safe in tourist areas. Be cautious at night in cities and use trusted taxi apps rather than hailing cabs. Verbal harassment can occur.
safety.notes: Romania is generally safe for tourists. Pickpocketing and taxi scams are the main concerns in Bucharest. Driving outside cities can be hazardous due to poor road conditions and wandering animals. Stray dogs remain an issue in rural areas.

practical.visaFreeCountries: EU/EEA citizens have free access. US, UK, Canada, Australia and many others can enter visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: May-September for warm weather and outdoor activities. December for Christmas markets in Bucharest, Cluj, and Sibiu. October for autumn foliage in the Carpathian Mountains.
